record.what_it_does: Marketing automation platform for email, SMS and customer data/CDP.
record.auth_notes: Server /api endpoints use a private API key (prefix pk_) sent as 'Authorization: Klaviyo-API-Key <key>'. Managing keys needs the Owner, Admin or Manager role. OAuth 2.0 with scopes is recommended for tech partners, and PKCE is required for both public and confidential clients. Client-side /client endpoints use a public key, the 6-char company/site ID. Outbound webhooks are signed with HMAC-SHA256.
record.access_notes: The free plan allows up to 250 active profiles and 500 emails per month. The pricing page does not tie API access to any plan. Owner, Admin and Manager roles can create private keys and OAuth apps. An OAuth app can be shared by installation URL without a listing. App Marketplace listing requires OAuth and review, and apps that ask for more scopes than needed are rejected. The Webhooks API is limited to Advanced KDP customers and Klaviyo app partners.
record.api_breadth_notes: A JSON:API-style REST API with date-versioned revisions. It covers profiles, lists, segments, events, metrics, campaigns, flows, templates, catalogs, coupons, reviews, tags, images, webhooks and more. That is well over 50 operations, but I did not count them exactly in the spec.
record.mcp_notes: Official remote server at https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp. It uses OAuth with dynamic client registration and is limited to the Owner, Admin and Manager roles. Klaviyo also documents a local server option.
record.blocker_notes: The REST API, OAuth (PKCE) and a free account and test account are all self-serve. Marketplace listing needs review but is not required, because apps can be distributed by installation URL. Managing webhook subscriptions through the API is limited to Advanced KDP customers and app partners. Klaviyo also runs an official remote MCP server.

evidence.quote: If you are a tech partner integrating with Klaviyo, we recommend using OAuth to make authorized API calls.
Private keys will have the prefix pk_ followed by a longer alphanumeric string.
All /client endpoints use a public API key: your 6-character company ID, also known as a site ID.
Your app does not have to be listed to share and use your installation URL with customers.
Note that only owner, admin, and manager roles can create OAuth apps in Klaviyo.
Up to 250 active profiles and 500 emails per month
test custom integrations and applications without any risk to your production account.
This feature is only available to Klaviyo users with an Owner, Admin, or Manager role.
Note that only Advanced KDP customers and Klaviyo app partners can access and manage webhooks with our Webhooks API.
